questions.question: Describe the features of IPv4 protocol. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the features of IPv4 protocol.
  • Ans. Internet Protocol version 4 (IPv4) is the fundamental protocol used for delivering packets
  • in a TCP/IP network. It provides a mechanism for logical addressing and routing of data across
  • interconnected networks.
  • One of the key features of IPv4 is that it is a connectionless protocol. This means that it does
  • not establish a dedicated path before transmitting data. Each packet, known as a datagram, is
  • sent independently and may follow different routes to reach the destination.
  • IPv4 is also an unreliable protocol because it does not guarantee the delivery of packets. Data
  • may be lost, duplicated, or arrive out of order. It follows a best-effort delivery approach, where
  • it attempts to deliver packets but provides no assurance of success. This is similar to a postal
  • service that tries to deliver mail but cannot guarantee delivery .
  • Another important feature is that IPv4 provides no flow control or error control, except for
  • basic error detection in the header. It does not handle congestion or retransmission of lost
  • packets. Instead, it relies on higher-level protocols such as TCP to ensure reliability and proper
  • sequencing.
  • IPv4 uses a datagram -based packet switching technique, where each packet is treated
  • independently . This allows efficient routing but may lead to packets arriving in different orders
  • or experiencing varying delays.
  • Finally , IPv4 provides logical addressing using 32 -bit addresses, which uniquely identify
  • devices on a network and enable routing across multiple interconnected networks.
  • In summary , IPv4 is a connectionless, unreliable, best -effort protocol that enables packet
  • delivery using logical addressing, while relying on higher -layer protocols for reliability and
  • control.

questions.question: Explain how a datagram network delivers packets without a dedicated path. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how a datagram network delivers packets without a dedicated path.
  • Ans. In a datagram network, packets are delivered without establishing a dedicated path
  • between the source and destination. This type of network follows a connectionless approach,
  • meaning there are no setup or teardown phases before or after transmission.
  • When a message is sent, it is first divided into smaller packets called datagrams. Each datagram
  • is treated as an independent unit, even if it is part of the same message. Every packet carries
  • the complete destination address, allowing it to be routed individually through the network.
  • In packet-switched networks, there is no resource reservation. This means that:
  • • No bandwidth is reserved in advance
  • • No fixed processing time is allocated
  • • Resources are assigned on a first-come, first-served basis
  • As each packet travels through the network, routers (packet switches) make independent
  • forwarding decisions based on current network conditions. Because of this, packets from the
  • same message may take different paths to reach the destination.
  • Due to the absence of a dedicated path and resource reservation:
  • • Packets may arrive out of order
  • • Packets may experience different delays
  • • Some packets may be lost or dropped due to congestion
  • The network itself does not ensure reliability . Instead, upper-layer protocols are responsible
  • for:
  • • Reordering packets
  • • Detecting lost packets
  • • Requesting retransmission
  • In summary , a datagram network delivers packets independently without a predefined path,
  • using dynamic routing and on-demand resource allocation, making it flexible but less reliable.

questions.question: Explain the role of protocol in a URL. / [CO4] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of protocol in a URL.
  • Ans. A Uniform Resource Locator (URL) is used to specify the address of a resource on th e
  • Internet. It consists of four main components: protocol, host, port, and path. Among these, the
  • protocol plays a crucial role in determining how the resource is accessed.
  • The protocol in a URL defines the client -server communication method used to retrie ve a
  • document. It specifies the set of rules and procedures that govern how data is transmitted
  • between the client (such as a web browser) and the server. In other words, the protocol tells the
  • system how to communicate with the host computer to obtain the required information.
  • Different protocols are used depending on the type of service required. For example, HTTP
  • (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the most commonly used protocol for accessing web pages,
  • while FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used for transferring files. The protocol is always placed
  • at the beginning of the URL, followed by a colon and slashes (e.g., http://), indicating the
  • method to be used for data retrieval.
  • The choice of protocol affects how the data is handled, including aspects such as data format,
  • connection type, and security . For instance, HTTP is used for standard web communicatio n,
  • while secure communication can use HTTPS.
  • In summary , the protocol in a URL specifies the type of service and communication rules
  • required to access a r esource, ensuring that the client and server interact correctly to retrieve
  • the requested information. [5 × 6 = 30]
